questions.text: Which technique is used to help mitigate SQL injection attacks?
options: using the same owner or admin account in the web applications to connect to the database
limiting the read access to specific fields of a table or joins of tables
using stored procedures with the "db_owner" default role
assigning DBA or admin access rights to the application account
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the damage a successful injection can do, so restricting read access to just the fields or joins the app needs is a mitigation. The other three options are things the course specifically warns against: a shared owner/admin account, db_owner on stored procedures, and DBA rights for the app account.

questions.text: Which security device is used to make responses to client requests look like they all come from the same server?
questions.explanation: A reverse proxy sits in front of many servers and makes every response look like it came from one server. A forward proxy is the mirror image: it makes requests from many clients look like they come from one client.

questions.text: What is a characteristic of a virtual machine running on a PC?
options: A virtual machine needs a physical network adapter to connect to the Internet.
A virtual machine runs its own operating system.
The number of virtual machines that can be made available depends on the software resources of the host machine.
A virtual machine is not susceptible to threats and malicious attacks.
questions.explanation: Each VM runs its own guest operating system. It reaches the network through a virtual adapter, how many VMs you can run depends on the host's hardware resources, and VMs are just as exposed to attacks as physical machines.

questions.text: What is a characteristic of the blue-green upgrade deployment strategy?
options: A new environment is created with the new code in it, while the old environment is held in reserve in case users experience problems.
The code changes are periodically rolled out in such a way that they do not impact current users.
The new code is deployed all at once to the old environment. If users experience no issues, it is then moved to the new environment.
The new code version is first rolled out to a subset of users. Changes can then be rolled back if the users experience any problems.
questions.explanation: Blue-green builds a complete new environment with the new code and switches traffic to it, keeping the old one on standby so traffic can be switched back if problems appear. Rolling out to a subset of users first is a canary deployment.

questions.text: Match the cloud model to its description. (Not all options are used.)

pairs.term: These are clouds that locate computing as close as possible to the user.
These clouds are made up of two or more clouds. However, each part remains a distinctive and separate object. Both of these are connected using a single architecture.
These are clouds that are intended for a specific organization or entity, such as the government. They can be set up using the private network of an organization.

questions.explanation: Edge clouds put compute as close to the user as possible. A hybrid cloud joins two or more clouds that stay separate but are managed through one architecture. A private cloud serves a single organisation. A public cloud, open to anyone, is the unused option.

questions.text: Which mitigation method is effective against cross-site scripting?
options: consistent hardening of systems and applications
using only necessary features and secure packages downloaded from official sources and verified with a signature
questions.explanation: XSS works by getting untrusted content rendered into a page, so the defence is to sanitize or escape that content wherever it's included. MFA and system hardening are good practice but don't stop injected script.

questions.text: Match the environments in the four-tier development environment structure to the description.

pairs.term: contains code that has been tested multiple times and is error free
includes automated tools such as Jenkins, CircleCI, or Travis CI, and is often integrated with a version control system
structurally as close to the actual production environment as possible

questions.explanation: Code moves development (where it's written) → testing (automated tools like Jenkins, wired to version control) → staging (built to mirror production for final acceptance) → production (tested, error-free code that real users run).

questions.text: Which attack involves the insertion of malicious code into SQL statements?
questions.explanation: SQL injection puts malicious SQL into an input that the server-side code then passes to the database without sanitising it. XSS injects script into web pages rather than queries.

questions.text: In software development, what is the purpose of a jump box?
options: to act as a single trusted machine used to launch connections to sensitive systems
to make all requests originating from within a network look like they come from the same source IP address
to filter packets based on Layer 3 and Layer 4 addressing
to receive incoming requests and forward them to multiple servers
questions.explanation: A jump box is a hardened, trusted host you have to log into first before connecting on to sensitive systems, which gives a single, auditable choke point. The other options describe a forward proxy, a packet filter and a load balancer/reverse proxy.

questions.text: Which characters are used to separate batched SQL statements?
questions.explanation: A batch is two or more SQL statements separated by semicolons. That's also why injected payloads so often contain ;, to tack an extra statement onto the end.

questions.text: What is a philosophy for software deployment used in the field of DevOps?
questions.explanation: CI/CD (continuous integration / continuous delivery or deployment) is the deployment philosophy at the heart of DevOps. OWASP is a security project, SOAP is a messaging protocol, and DevNet is Cisco's developer program.

questions.text: Which statement is a characteristic of the broken access control threat to web applications?
options: It allows attackers to access, and potentially change, serialized versions of data and objects.
It allows an attacker to use the dynamic functions of a site to inject malicious content into the page.
It allows users to circumvent existing authentication requirements.
It allows attackers to steal sensitive information such as passwords or personal information.
questions.explanation: Broken access control lets users get around authentication or authorization checks and reach things they shouldn't. The other options describe insecure deserialization, XSS and sensitive data exposure.

questions.text: Which technology is used to containerize applications and allows them to run in a variety of environments?
questions.explanation: Docker packages an application and everything it needs into a container that runs the same in almost any environment. VirtualBox runs full virtual machines, not containers.

questions.text: Match the OWASP resource with a description.

pairs.term: explains ways to mitigate command security issues in web applications
looks for known vulnerabilities in code
generic attack detection rules used with web application firewalls

questions.explanation: OWASP Dependency-Check flags known-vulnerable components, DefectDojo streamlines testing and vulnerability management, the ModSecurity Core Rule Set gives a WAF its generic attack-detection rules, and the Cheat Sheet Series is guidance on mitigating specific issues.

questions.text: What is used to isolate the different parts of a running container?
questions.explanation: Namespaces give each container its own isolated view of processes, network, mounts and so on. Control groups limit resources (CPU, memory) rather than isolate, and union file systems build the layered image.
